source_refs.note: Topic 25.3.1 (PDF 234); Figures 25.4 and 25.6 are combined in an original diagram. The book lists crabs, vultures and jackals as decomposers and detritivores; they are detritivores or scavengers, decomposers being mainly bacteria and fungi.

blocks.text: In an ecosystem organisms are arranged in feeding groups called trophic levels.

items: Trophic level 1: green plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria, the primary producers.
Trophic level 2: primary consumers (herbivores) that feed directly on producers, such as insects and rabbits.
Trophic level 3: secondary consumers (carnivores) and animal parasites that feed on herbivores, such as frogs and snakes.
Trophic level 4: tertiary consumers, animals that eat carnivores, such as wolves and hawks.
Decomposers and detritivores (crabs, vultures and jackals) form a separate level that feeds on all the others, consuming detritus (dead, decaying material) and faecal matter.

blocks.alt: Four stacked pictures joined by orange upward arrows: trophic level 1, ferns; trophic level 2, a grasshopper; trophic level 3, a mouse; trophic level 4, an eagle. A yellow arrow from the Sun points to trophic level 1. Thin arrows lead from every level to a pink oval of decomposers (mushroom, bacteria and other microbes).
